title: $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ agrees with the divisor module of file 06
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $C$ a smooth connected curve over $k$ and $D=\sum_{i=1}^m n_i[P_i]$ a divisor of $C$ which is an effective Cartier divisor (so the coefficients are nonnegative). Then the module $\mathcal{O}_C(D)$ of [def-sc-divisor] (a sub-$\mathcal{O}_C$-module of the constant sheaf $k(C)$) and the module $\mathcal{O}_C(D)$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] are canonically isomorphic.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], $C$ is integral with function field $k(C)$ and each closed-point local ring is a discrete valuation ring. By [lem-sc-point-cartier], the effective divisor $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor, and locally at each $P_i$ its ideal is generated by $t_i^{n_i}$ for a uniformizer $t_i$; away from the support of $D$ the ideal is the unit ideal.

On an open $U$ where the ideal of $D$ is principal, say $\mathcal{I}_D=f\mathcal{O}_U$ with $f\in k(C)^*$, a homomorphism $\mathcal{I}_D|_U\to\mathcal{O}_U$ is determined by the image of $f$, and $a\mapsto a/f$ identifies $\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal{I}_D,\mathcal{O}_C)|_U$ with $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_U$ inside $k(C)$; this is the module of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] by its definition. The identification is valid because multiplication by the non-zero-divisor $f$ is injective.

For every open $V\subseteq U$, [lem-sc-divisor-module-local] identifies the module of [def-sc-divisor] with $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_C(V)$, while step 2 identifies the dual ideal module with the same submodule of $k(C)$. These local identifications agree on overlaps because all restriction maps are inclusions into $k(C)$, so they glue to a canonical isomorphism of the two $\mathcal{O}_C$-modules.
